notes: This source/test traceability contract records Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 default-region realization in the non-installable embedded development profile. The RTI keeps the default region as derived, invisible state rather than inventing a public RegionHandle; it applies it to active object discovery/scope/reflection, ordinary and regional interaction routing, update-rate relevance, source association replacement/restoration, and receive-order and timestamped callback metadata. The Catch2 cases prove receive-order behavior, direct time-constrained timestamped object reflection and interaction delivery, default-source object and interaction mixed fanout, a default-source interaction delivered through Flush Queue before FQG, default-source interaction delivery through the inclusive TARA and NMRA boundaries, default-source timestamped object and interaction updates delivered through the shared FQR/TARA/NMRA frontier, and default-source object and interaction queues that survive a Time Constrained disable/re-enable cycle: each regional callback carries the supplied-empty RegionHandleSet while the derived default source remains private. A focused untimed save/restore companion now reconstructs one queued default-source timestamped interaction, its supplied-empty callback projection, and live retraction ledger through restore before Flush Queue delivery and Request Retraction. A timed companion retains a timestamp-eight default-source attribute passel across a timestamp-six save boundary before restore and FQR delivery; RL-141 records the missing cross-service save-boundary relation. They do not independently validate the remaining timestamped default-region/re-enable matrix beyond these bounded role transitions, relaxed DDM, all dimension/attribute combinations, distributed transport, durable save/restore, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, or conformance.
